docs.title: Yaas — Yet Another Audio Splitter
docs.text:
Yaas is a desktop application that splits a YouTube video's soundtrack into separate stems (vocals, drums, bass, other, ...).

It works by:

  1. embedding a browser so you can navigate to and pick a YouTube video,
  2. downloading its audio and converting it to FLAC,
  3. splitting the FLAC into stems using a machine-learning source-separation model (either OpenUnmix or audio-separator),
  4. writing the resulting WAV stems to an output directory ($HOME/yaas_tracks by default).

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• New to Yaas? Start with Installation.
  • Already installed it? See Usage for how to run an extraction and choose a separation backend.
  • Want to build Yaas from source, package an installer, or cut a release? See Building & Releasing.

docs.title: Copyright and licensing
docs.text:
Respect the copyright of the video authors. If they don't authorize redistribution, keep your extracted stems for personal use only.

Yaas is free software, licensed under the Mozilla Public License 2.0 (MPL 2.0). It includes parts of the youtube-to-mp3 project, also under the MPL license.

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text:
Yaas uses uv for environment and dependency management. A .venv lives at the repo root.

# Run from source without installing
python -m yaas

# or, once installed in the environment
yaas

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
The tests use pytest, and need no network access nor display:

uv pip install --group dev
pytest

YAAS_SLOW_TESTS=1 pytest also runs a real OpenUnmix separation, which downloads its model on first use.

docs.title: Linting
docs.text:
CI runs flake8, then the tests, the same way you can locally:

flake8 . --count --select=E9,F63,F7,F82 --show-source --statistics
flake8 . --count --exit-zero --max-complexity=10 --max-line-length=127 --statistics

docs.title: Cutting a release
docs.text:
Versioning is managed by bumpver, which keeps pyproject.toml, src/yaas/__init__.py, README.md, and inno_setup_script.iss in sync.

git commit
bumpver update --patch   # or --minor / --major

Pushing the version tag that bumpver creates triggers the release workflows on GitHub Actions:

  • publish.yml builds the sdist/wheel and publishes them to PyPI using Trusted Publishing (no API token needed).
  • release.yml builds installers for Windows, macOS, and Linux and attaches them to the corresponding GitHub Release:
    • Windows: PyInstaller (yaas.spec) + Inno Setup (inno_setup_script.iss) → yaas_installer.exe.
    • macOS: PyInstaller + hdiutil → yaas_installer.dmg (unsigned).
    • Linux: PyInstaller + appimagetool → yaas-x86_64.AppImage (best-effort — this job is allowed to fail without blocking the rest of the release).

docs.title: Building installers locally
docs.text:
WindowsmacOSLinux (AppImage) 
pyinstaller .\yaas.spec
& 'C:\Program Files (x86)\Inno Setup 6\ISCC.exe' .\inno_setup_script.iss

pyinstaller yaas.spec
hdiutil create -volname Yaas -srcfolder dist/yaas.app -ov -format UDZO yaas_installer.dmg

pyinstaller yaas.spec
# Package dist/yaas/ into an AppDir, then:
./appimagetool-x86_64.AppImage AppDir yaas-x86_64.AppImage

New features:

  • Job queue: while a job runs, Add to Queue prepares the next ones, which then run in order. The job list shows each job's state, with actions on right-click.
  • Playlists: a playlist page's videos are all split, one after the other.
  • Links to the written stems in the status log, and an Open Output Folder menu entry.
  • Progress is also shown while downloading the video and the model.
  • More YouTube URLs are recognized: youtu.be, Shorts, live videos, m.youtube.com and YouTube Music.
  • --version option.
  • Stems are written at 48 kHz by default, the usual rate of DAW sessions, which then don't have to convert them on import. The models still work at 44.1 kHz; the stems are resampled afterwards. 44.1 kHz can be chosen in Settings..., or for one run with --sample-rate.

Fixes:

  • Stop now stops the job immediately and cleanly, at any step, instead of abruptly killing the thread: the separation runs in a child process, which Stop ends, and the job's intermediate files are removed. An interrupted model download no longer leaves a truncated model behind. The button is red.
  • GPU acceleration on Windows: the GPU environment got PyPI's CPU-only PyTorch. It now gets PyTorch's CUDA build (CUDA 13 for Blackwell GPUs).
  • OpenUnmix produces stereo stems (they were mono), and is given the audio's actual sample rate.
  • The audio is decoded straight to FLAC, without the lossy MP3 step, which degraded the separation's input.
  • A failed step no longer reports "Extraction complete", and errors are reported once, with their cause.
  • Closing Yaas during a job no longer crashes it.

Other changes:

  • Removed the unused ffmpeg PyPI dependency (Yaas uses the ffmpeg program).
  • Test suite, run by CI.

Yaas is versioned with bumpver and released via tagged GitHub Releases.

See the GitHub Releases page for the full history of published versions and their artifacts, and the commit history for day-to-day changes.

docs.title: Windows: using the installer
docs.text:
If you are on Windows and don't want to deal with Python packaging, grab the latest yaas_installer.exe from the GitHub Releases page and run it.

You also need ffmpeg installed. The simplest way on Windows is with winget (installed by default on Windows 11; available via the Microsoft Store on older versions). From PowerShell:

winget install ffmpeg

docs.title: macOS: using the installer
docs.text:
Grab the latest yaas_installer.dmg from the GitHub Releases page, open it, and drag Yaas into /Applications.

Apple Silicon only

This build is arm64-only (Apple Silicon: M1/M2/M3/...) — GitHub retired its free Intel macOS build runners, and no free CI service fills the gap. On an Intel Mac, install via uv pip install yaas / pip install yaas instead (see below).

Unsigned application

This build isn't signed or notarized by an Apple Developer account, so Gatekeeper will warn that it's from an "unidentified developer" the first time you open it. Right-click the app and choose Open (instead of double-clicking) to bypass that warning once.

ffmpeg is included in the app: there's nothing else to install. (These are the static FFmpeg builds by Martin Riedl, licensed under the GPL and shipped as separate, unmodified programs.)

docs.title: Linux: using the AppImage
docs.text:
Grab the latest yaas-x86_64.AppImage from the GitHub Releases page, make it executable, and run it:

chmod +x yaas-x86_64.AppImage
./yaas-x86_64.AppImage

Install ffmpeg with your distribution's package manager, e.g. on Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt install ffmpeg.

docs.title: Any platform: using uv / pip
docs.text:
Create and activate a virtual environment. See the uv documentation if you're not familiar with it.

Then install Yaas into that environment:

uv pip install yaas

On Windows, make sure you also have a working Python installation and ffmpeg installed (see above).

docs.title: GPU acceleration
docs.text:
The packaged Windows and Linux installers above bundle a CPU-only build of PyTorch (a CUDA-enabled build alone exceeds GitHub Releases' 2GB per-file limit), so track separation runs on CPU by default regardless of your hardware. The macOS installer is different: see GPU acceleration on macOS below.

Installing via uv pip install yaas / pip install yaas instead pulls the regular PyPI PyTorch build. On Linux, it automatically uses a compatible CUDA GPU when one is available and falls back to CPU otherwise. On Windows, PyPI's PyTorch is CPU-only: install a CUDA build from PyTorch's own index into the same environment, for example:

uv pip install torch torchaudio torchvision torchcodec --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126

docs.title: Enabling GPU acceleration in the Windows/Linux installers
docs.text:
If you installed Yaas via the Windows or Linux packaged installer and have an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA support, open the ☰ menu and choose GPU Acceleration..., then Install. This downloads a separate, self-contained Python environment with CUDA-enabled PyTorch (several GB) that Yaas then uses automatically for extraction whenever it's present. Use the same menu entry later to check its status, reinstall it (e.g. after upgrading Yaas), or remove it.

Yaas installs the CUDA 12.6 build of PyTorch, which supports the widest range of NVIDIA GPUs and drivers, or the CUDA 13 build when nvidia-smi reports a Blackwell GPU (RTX 50xx), which needs it (and an NVIDIA driver 580 or newer).

docs.title: GPU acceleration on macOS
docs.text: Apple hardware has no CUDA support, but on Apple Silicon Macs (M1 and later) Yaas uses the GPU through Apple's Metal (MPS) backend out of the box, with both the macOS dmg installer and pip install yaas. There's nothing extra to download. The ☰ menu's GPU Acceleration... entry shows whether Metal acceleration is available on your Mac.

docs.title: Installed with the Windows installer
docs.text: Search for "Yaas" in your installed applications and start it.

docs.title: Installed with the macOS installer or the Linux AppImage
docs.text: Launch it like any other application (from /Applications on macOS, or by running the .AppImage file on Linux).

docs.title: Installed with uv / pip
docs.text:
Activate your virtual environment and run:

yaas

docs.title: Extracting stems
docs.text:
1. Use the embedded browser to search for or navigate to the video you want. A playlist page (youtube.com/playlist?list=...) works too: all its videos are split, one after the other.
  2. Click Start.
  3. Wait — separation can take a while, especially on CPU. The progress bar follows the download, the model download on first use, and the separation itself.
  4. When the job is done, the status log lists the written stems: click one to open it. They're in the output folder set in Settings... ($HOME/yaas_tracks by default; --out overrides it for a single run without changing the saved setting), which Open Output Folder in the ☰ menu also opens.

docs.title: Queueing jobs
docs.text:
You don't have to wait for a job to finish to prepare the next one: while one runs, keep browsing, and click Add to Queue (the Start button's label while a job runs) on each video you want. Queued jobs run one at a time, in order, each with the output folder and model set when it was queued.

The job list, left of the status log, shows each job's state. Right-click a job to remove it from the queue, open its output folder or show it in the browser again, or to clear the finished jobs. Double-clicking a finished job opens its output folder.

docs.title: Stopping a job
docs.text:
Click the red Stop button to stop the running job, whatever it's doing (downloading, separating, or downloading a model); the next queued one then starts. The separation runs in a separate process, which Stop ends immediately. Stems already written are kept.

Closing Yaas while a job runs asks for confirmation, then stops it and drops the queued jobs.

Note

Respect the copyright of the video's authors. If they don't authorize sharing, keep your extracted stems for personal use only.

docs.title: The menu
docs.text:
The ☰ button to the right of the URL bar opens a menu with:

  • Settings... — set the output folder extracted stems are written to, picked via your system's native folder picker, the separation model (see below), and the stems' sample rate: 48 kHz (default) or 44.1 kHz. The models work at 44.1 kHz; 48 kHz stems are resampled afterwards, so that DAWs working at 48 kHz can import them without converting them.
  • Open Output Folder — opens the output folder in your file manager.
  • Documentation — opens this site in your browser.
  • Report an Issue — opens the GitHub issue tracker.
  • GPU Acceleration... — on Windows/Linux, install, reinstall, or remove an on-demand CUDA-accelerated environment; see Installation. On Apple Silicon Macs, shows whether the built-in Metal (MPS) acceleration is available; see Installation.
  • About Yaas — shows the installed version and license.

docs.title: Choosing a separation backend
docs.text:
Pick the separation model in Settings...: BS-Roformer (default), HTDemucs 6 stems, or OpenUnmix. The choice is saved for future runs. It can also be overridden for a single run from the command line.

Yaas supports two backends for splitting the soundtrack into stems:

  1. audio-separator (default) — uses the audio-separator library. Choose a model with --model:
    • roformer (default)
    • htdemucs6s
  2. OpenUnmix — uses the OpenUnmix model.
# audio-separator with a specific model
yaas --backend audio_separator --model htdemucs6s

# OpenUnmix backend
yaas --backend openunmix

docs.title: Command-line options
docs.text: Option Default Description --version Print Yaas' version and exit. -o, --out DIR Settings dialog's output folder Directory to store the output files in, for this run only. --backend {audio_separator,openunmix} Settings dialog's model Track separation backend, for this run only. --model {roformer,htdemucs6s} Settings dialog's model Model used by the audio_separator backend, for this run only. --sample-rate {44100,48000} Settings dialog's sample rate (48000) Sample rate of the written stems, for this run only.

docs.title: Testing on Windows in a VM
docs.text:
How to run a manual test pass of the Windows installer on a Linux machine, with no prior experience of virtual machines. It assumes Ubuntu and an x86_64 CPU.

CI already builds the installer and runs --self-test on real Windows. This pass covers what CI doesn't: the installer, the embedded browser, real separations, Stop, and a user account with accents in its name.

Not covered: CUDA. It needs an NVIDIA GPU passed through to the VM, so test it on a real Windows machine with an NVIDIA card.

The steps use quickemu, a small wrapper around QEMU/KVM:

  • QEMU emulates a PC, KVM makes it fast, and quickemu picks the settings.
  • A VM is just a folder and a config file. Deleting them removes it.
  • Its networking doesn't use a bridge, so it works next to Docker and UFW, which can cut a VM's internet access under libvirt/virt-manager.
  • quickget installs Windows unattended, including the VirtIO drivers and a local account, so no Microsoft account is needed.

Allow about 1 hour for the setup (mostly unattended) and 1 to 3 hours for the test pass, since separation on CPU is slow.

docs.title: Disk use
docs.text:
Everything goes on the host disk, in the folder you create in step 2. Sizes marked ~ are estimates; the others come from the 1.0.0 release and from model files downloaded on Linux.

Item Size Notes quickemu and its dependencies ~100 MB apt shows the exact figure Windows ISO ~8 GB Can be deleted after install (step 5) VirtIO drivers ISO ~750 MB Can be deleted after install (step 5) VM disk (disk.qcow2), fresh Windows ~25 GB Grows as needed, up to about 64 GB Windows updates ~5-10 GB Inside the VM disk Snapshot starts near 0 Grows as Windows rewrites data after it's taken

Yaas uses this inside the VM disk:

Item Size Notes Installer 531 MiB Installed yaas.exe ~530 MiB Extraction to %TEMP%\_MEI* ~3.6 GB While running; based on a Linux build; see the note below BS-Roformer model 699 MB Kept in the cache OpenUnmix model 452 MB Kept in the cache HTDemucs 6 stems model ~55 MB Kept in the cache Browser cache ~250 MB ffmpeg ~500 MB Stems for a 4-minute song 180-550 MB 4 to 6 WAV files, depending on model and format GPU environment (optional) several GB Skip it: no use without an NVIDIA GPU

Yaas's single-file build unpacks itself to %TEMP% at each launch and removes that copy on a clean exit. A killed or crashed yaas can leave ~3.6 GB behind, which the test pass checks.

Budget 60 GB free before starting. A full pass should stay around 45-55 GB, but check with du -sh as you go. The VM disk never shrinks by itself, even if you delete files inside Windows; deleting the VM (step 8) gets it all back.

If you back up your home folder, exclude the VM folder.

docs.title: 1. Check the host and install quickemu
docs.text:
df -h ~                       # at least 60 GB available
ls -l /dev/kvm                # must exist
test -r /dev/kvm -a -w /dev/kvm && echo "KVM OK" || echo "no KVM access"
sudo apt install quickemu

If /dev/kvm is missing, enable virtualization (VT-x or AMD-V) in the BIOS/UEFI settings. If it exists but you have no access, run sudo usermod -aG kvm "$USER", then log out and back in.

On a recent Intel CPU with performance and efficiency cores, Windows guests can hang or crash on low-level CPU register accesses that KVM doesn't handle. Have KVM ignore them (quickemu also warns about this setting at startup). This lasts until the host reboots, so run it again after a reboot:

echo Y | sudo tee /sys/module/kvm/parameters/ignore_msrs

To make it permanent, use echo "options kvm ignore_msrs=Y" | sudo tee /etc/modprobe.d/kvm-quickemu.conf.

docs.title: 2. Download Windows and create the VM
docs.text:
mkdir -p ~/VMs && cd ~/VMs
quickget windows 11

This downloads the Windows 11 ISO from Microsoft and the VirtIO drivers, then creates windows-11.conf and a windows-11/ folder. A different language can be requested, e.g. quickget windows 11 "French".

This is the regular Windows 11 ISO, not the 90-day evaluation. It runs unactivated, showing a watermark and with personalization settings locked, which doesn't affect the tests. Microsoft's license terms still expect a license for it; if that matters for your use, see Using the 90-day evaluation instead.

If Microsoft blocks the download, quickget says so and still creates the VM. In that case:

  1. Get the "Windows 11 Disk Image (ISO) for x64 devices" from https://www.microsoft.com/software-download/windows11 in a browser.
  2. Save it as ~/VMs/windows-11/windows-11.iso.

Now give the VM more resources than the defaults, as separation is heavy. Adjust these to your machine, leaving the host enough to work with:

cat >> windows-11.conf <<'EOF'
ram="16G"
cpu_cores="8"
EOF

docs.title: 3. Install Windows
docs.text:
quickemu --vm windows-11.conf

A window opens and Windows installs itself, restarting a few times. Don't interact with it unless it stops at a question. This takes about 20-40 minutes. It ends on the desktop, logged in as user Quickemu, password quickemu.

To use the VM window:

  • Click inside to capture the mouse and keyboard, and press Ctrl+Alt+G to release them.
  • There's no copy and paste with the host in this default display mode, so URLs below are kept short.
  • Shut down from the Windows Start menu, which also closes the VM.
  • The keyboard follows the layout set in Windows, not the host's: US QWERTY at first. On an AZERTY keyboard, type quickemu as if on QWERTY (q is the A key, m is the , key), or add your layout in Settings > Time & language > Language & region.

If quickemu reports a TPM or swtpm permission error (AppArmor can block it on Ubuntu), change tpm="on" to tpm="off" in windows-11.conf. The unattended install skips Windows 11's TPM check, and yaas doesn't need a TPM.

docs.title: 4. Prepare a test account
docs.text:
Yaas should work for a user whose name has accents and a space, since these end up in its data paths. In the VM, right-click Start, open Terminal (Admin), and run:

$name = "$([char]0xC9)lo$([char]0xEF)se Test"    # "Éloïse Test", on any keyboard
$pw = Read-Host -AsSecureString "Password for the test account"
New-LocalUser -Name $name -Password $pw
Add-LocalGroupMember -Group "Users" -Member $name

Then, still as Quickemu:

  1. Run Settings > Windows Update until no more updates are offered, then choose Pause updates, so they don't eat disk or CPU during the tests.
  2. Sign out, log in once as Éloïse Test so that the profile gets created, and wait a few minutes: this is also when winget becomes available to this user.
  3. Shut down from the Start menu.

docs.title: 5. Free the ISOs and take a clean snapshot
docs.text:
The ISOs aren't needed anymore. Remove their lines from the config, then delete them:

cd ~/VMs
sed -i -E '/^(iso|fixed_iso)=/d' windows-11.conf
du -h windows-11/*.iso                  # see what you're about to delete
rm windows-11/*.iso
du -sh windows-11                       # current size of the VM

Now save this clean state, before ffmpeg and yaas exist on it. With the VM shut down:

quickemu --vm windows-11.conf --snapshot create clean

To retest from scratch later (for example on a new build), go back to it:

quickemu --vm windows-11.conf --snapshot apply clean

docs.title: 6. Get the installer into the VM
docs.text:
Start the VM with quickemu --vm windows-11.conf and log in as Éloïse Test.

Published release: open Edge in the VM and go to the releases page, https://github.com/kleag/yaas/releases, then download yaas_installer.exe. This is what users do, so it also shows you the warnings they get.

Unreleased code: build it with the release workflow from the branch you pushed, which takes a while and creates no release. On the host:

gh workflow run release.yml --ref <branch>
gh run list --workflow=release.yml --limit 1     # note the run's ID
gh run watch <run-id>
gh run download <run-id> -n yaas_installer_windows -D ~/VMs/build
python3 -m http.server --bind 127.0.0.1 8000 -d ~/VMs/build

Then, in Edge in the VM, go to http://10.0.2.2:8000/yaas_installer.exe. From inside the VM, 10.0.2.2 is the host's localhost. Stop the server with Ctrl+C when done.

docs.title: 7. Run the test pass
docs.text:
Choose a short video of 2-3 minutes: a CPU separation can take far longer than the song. A slow or stuttering YouTube video isn't a yaas bug, as the VM has no GPU acceleration.

Expected data locations (if one differs, note it and search for yaas under %APPDATA% and %LOCALAPPDATA%):

What Where Job temp folders %APPDATA%\yaas\work audio-separator models %LOCALAPPDATA%\yaas\cache\audio-separator-models OpenUnmix models %USERPROFILE%\.cache\torch\hub\checkpoints Stems %USERPROFILE%\yaas_tracks

docs.title: Install, without ffmpeg
docs.text:
• [ ] Note any Edge or SmartScreen warning. On "Windows protected your PC", choose More info > Run anyway.
  • [ ] The installer asks for admin rights (user Quickemu, password quickemu) and finishes.
  • [ ] Start Yaas from the Start menu: a "FFMPEG Check" error appears, and the app exits cleanly. Note how long startup takes (a single-file build is slow, and Defender scans it).

docs.title: Install ffmpeg as the README says
docs.text:
• [ ] In a terminal, winget install ffmpeg succeeds.
  • [ ] Yaas now starts from the Start menu, with no error. If it still reports no ffmpeg, retry after signing out and in, and note this: the README would need to mention it.

docs.title: Self-test
docs.text:
• [ ] In PowerShell, this ends with Self-test passed and 0:
$p = Start-Process "$env:ProgramFiles\YAAS\yaas.exe" -ArgumentList '--self-test',"$env:USERPROFILE\selftest.txt" -Wait -PassThru
Get-Content "$env:USERPROFILE\selftest.txt"
$p.ExitCode

docs.title: Window and browser
docs.text:
• [ ] The window icon and title are right; resizing works.
  • [ ] YouTube loads, the cookie prompt can be answered, a video plays with sound.
  • [ ] Typing in YouTube's search box works.
  • [ ] ☰ menu: Settings..., Open Output Folder, Documentation, Report an Issue and About Yaas (right version) all work.

docs.title: Separation
docs.text:
For each model, chosen in Settings...: click Start on your video.

  • [ ] BS-Roformer: the model download shows progress, then separation does, and WAV files appear.
  • [ ] HTDemucs 6 stems: produces 6 files, including guitar and piano.
  • [ ] OpenUnmix: produces 4 files.
  • [ ] Each stem link in the status log opens in the default player, and it sounds right.
  • [ ] A WAV's Properties > Details shows the sample rate from Settings (48 kHz by default).
  • [ ] %APPDATA%\yaas\work is empty after each job.
  • [ ] Second run of a model: no new download.

docs.title: Paths
docs.text:
• [ ] In Settings..., an output folder with a space and an accent (e.g. Documents\Mes morceaux é) works, and Open Output Folder opens it.
  • [ ] A video whose title has characters forbidden in Windows file names (: ? " / | *) or non-Latin ones produces stems, with usable links.

docs.title: Stop
docs.text:
• [ ] Stop during the download: job ends as cancelled, temp folder removed.
  • [ ] Stop during separation: the status changes promptly, Task Manager shows no separation process left working (only the main yaas.exe processes, with CPU near 0), and the work folder gets emptied. "File in use" problems, which Linux doesn't have, would show here.
  • [ ] Stop during a first-time model download (delete the model from the cache to test), then Start again: it downloads again and works.
  • [ ] A new job after each Stop works.

docs.title: Queue and playlist
docs.text:
• [ ] While a job runs, browse to another video and click Add to Queue: the jobs run in order.
  • [ ] Remove a queued job with a right-click.
  • [ ] A short playlist produces stems for each of its videos.

docs.title: Closing and leftovers
docs.text:
• [ ] Close the window with a job running: yaas.exe and its child processes disappear from Task Manager within a few seconds.
  • [ ] Look for _MEI* folders in %TEMP%, and note their size. Clean exits should leave none; note whether a close during a job, or killing yaas from Task Manager, leaves them, and whether they pile up over launches.
  • [ ] After such a close, the next launch works, and stale work folders get removed.

docs.title: GPU dialog (no NVIDIA GPU)
docs.text: • [ ] ☰ > GPU Acceleration... opens and reads sensibly. Click Cancel. Installing downloads several GB and can only end with "no CUDA-capable GPU detected", so skip it unless you're testing this message.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
• [ ] Settings > Apps > Installed apps > Yaas > Uninstall removes it, and the Start menu entry. Note what's left in %APPDATA%, %LOCALAPPDATA%, %USERPROFILE%\.cache and yaas_tracks.
  • [ ] Reinstalling works.

docs.title: 8. Clean up
docs.text:
Keep the VM, and its snapshot, as long as you might retest. If disk space runs low, go back to the clean snapshot (step 5), or delete it once you no longer need it, with --snapshot delete clean. Snapshot data inside the file may not return to the host, though, so only deleting the VM is sure to free the space.

To delete everything:

cd ~/VMs
quickemu --vm windows-11.conf --delete-vm    # deletes the windows-11 folder and config
rm -rf ~/VMs/build                           # if you used it
du -sh ~/VMs
sudo apt remove quickemu                     # optional; `sudo apt autoremove` for its dependencies

docs.title: Using the 90-day evaluation instead
docs.text:
Microsoft offers a Windows 11 Enterprise evaluation, free after registration. It costs more effort, as the unattended install doesn't apply:

  • Its page says that you must sign in with a Microsoft account. Have one ready.
  • Choose the regular ISO, not LTSC: LTSC has no Microsoft Store, and so no winget, which the README relies on.
  • After 90 days, the desktop turns black and the PC shuts down every hour, so recreate the VM rather than keeping it.

Follow step 2, which still sets up the VM and the drivers, and save the evaluation ISO in ~/VMs/windows-11/. Then make the VM use it for a manual install, removing the regular ISO if quickget downloaded it:

cd ~/VMs
ls -lh windows-11/*.iso
rm windows-11/unattended.iso
rm windows-11/Win11*.iso                # the regular ISO, if there's one
sed -i 's|^iso=.*|iso="windows-11/your-evaluation.iso"|' windows-11.conf
quickemu --vm windows-11.conf

Windows setup then asks its questions, and won't see the disk at first: choose Load driver, and browse the VirtIO CD to viostor\w11\amd64.

The account sign-in needs internet, but the network card has no driver yet. On the "connect to a network" screen, look for an option to install a driver, and browse to NetKVM\w11\amd64 on the same CD. This screen changes between Windows releases, and these steps haven't been tried on the current one.

After the install, run virtio-win-gt-x64.msi from the CD for the other drivers. Then go on with step 4, substituting your own admin account for Quickemu.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem What to do Windows hangs or blue-screens at boot or during install Check cat /sys/module/kvm/parameters/ignore_msrs shows Y (step 1), then start the VM again winget isn't recognized Wait a few minutes after the first login. If it persists, run Add-AppxPackage -RegisterByFamilyName -MainPackage Microsoft.DesktopAppInstaller_8wekyb3d8bbwe Edge blocks the http://10.0.2.2 download Choose Keep in the downloads list Very slow VM Check that quickemu's startup output doesn't complain about KVM, and lower cpu_cores if the host is starving Stuck on a boot screen or UEFI shell during install Close the VM and run quickemu --vm windows-11.conf again The display freezes The default display (sdl) is the safe one; quickemu's wiki reports freezes with --display spice on Windows guests Separation killed, or out-of-memory errors Raise ram in windows-11.conf, with the VM shut down Windows disk full Delete stems, models and %TEMP%\_MEI* folders in the VM, or go back to the snapshot Host disk running full Shut down the VM and see Clean up VM asks for activation Expected, with the regular ISO; ignore it
